chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about wearing al-firā', al-sammūr, al-fanak, foxes, and all skins. He said: There is no harm.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as a kind of taqiyyah, as we have explained in other reports, because no one agrees with us on that. And it is possible that his statement, “there is no harm in it,” is specific to some of what the question included, namely al-sinjāb, because permission has been given for salat in it, as we have explained in some reports. And it may be that in the answer regarding what is other than al-sinjāb, he relied upon what had already preceded from him and from his forefathers عليهم السلام of clarification. As for al-sammūr in particular, it also indicates its reprehensibility.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in expressing a ruling
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable fur, discussed here as particularly disliked
key_terms.السِّنْجَابُ: squirrel fur, treated here as an exception permitted in salat
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act for which the legal ruling is especially relevant
key_terms.الْجُلُودِ: skins or hides generally included in the question
key_terms.الْفَنَكِ: fanak fur, one of the animal furs mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: fur garments mentioned in the question
key_terms.لِبَاسِ: garment or clothing being asked about in legal context

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith on praying in furs such as al-fanak, al-sammur, and al-sinjab understood in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report asks Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about garments made from certain furs and skins, and the reply given is that there is no harm in them. The accompanying discussion explains that this answer is either to be understood as taqiyyah or as restricted to al-sinjāb, for which permission in salat is established in other reports, while al-sammūr in particular is indicated to be disliked.
